title: PERKS: a Locality-Optimized Execution Model for Iterative Memory-bound GPU Applications
authors: Lingqi Zhang; Mohamed Wahib; Peng Chen; Jintao Meng; Xiao Wang; Toshio Endo; Satoshi Matsuoka
affiliations: Tokyo Institute of Technology, RIKEN Center for Computational Science, AIST, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (CAS), Oak Ridge National Laboratory
research_focus: Roofline analysis, Performance modeling, Hardware co-design, GPU memory tiering

problem_statement.en: Iterative memory-bound GPU solvers (stencils, Krylov/CG) are bottlenecked by repeated round-trips to device memory: the standard pattern launches one kernel per time step, so every iteration writes the full output back to global memory and reads it again next step, wasting the kernel-launch/barrier overhead and saturating HBM bandwidth even though much of the working set could stay on-chip across iterations.
problem_statement.zh: 迭代式且受記憶體頻寬限制的 GPU 解算器（stencil、Krylov/CG）的瓶頸在於對 device memory 的反覆往返：標準作法是每個時間步啟動一個 kernel，因此每次迭代都把完整輸出寫回 global memory、下一步再讀回，浪費了 kernel 啟動與 barrier 開銷，並把 HBM 頻寬打滿——即使大部分工作集其實可以跨迭代留在晶片上。

key_innovation.en: PERKS (PERsistent KernelS): move the time loop *inside* a single persistent kernel that spans the whole device and uses grid-wide (cooperative-groups) barriers for inter-iteration synchronization instead of relaunching. The freed-up on-chip capacity — leftover registers and shared memory not needed for peak occupancy — is then used to cache a subset of each step's output across iterations, cutting device-memory traffic. The scheme is solver-agnostic and orthogonal to the solver's own kernel math.
key_innovation.zh: PERKS（PERsistent KernelS）：把時間迴圈搬進單一、橫跨整個 device 的 persistent kernel，以 grid 層級（cooperative-groups）barrier 做跨迭代同步，取代反覆重啟 kernel。接著把省下來的晶片內容量——達到尖峰 occupancy 後仍有餘裕的 register 與 shared memory——用來跨迭代快取每一步輸出的子集，藉此削減 device memory 流量。此機制與解算器無關，且與解算器本身的 kernel 數學正交。

reported_accuracy: Not Reported (this is an execution model + roofline analysis, not a latency-prediction model; speedups are measured, not predicted)
validation_workloads: 2D/3D iterative stencils (Jacobi etc.), Krylov-subspace Conjugate Gradient over SuiteSparse SpMV matrices

scope_assumptions.en: Targets iterative memory-bound (bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound) kernels whose working set does not need all registers/shared memory for peak performance; reuse capacity is bounded by leftover on-chip SRAM, so problems must fit (or be tiled to fit) the cacheable subset. Relies on grid-wide cooperative-group barriers (persistent grid must fit on one device). Single-GPU; no multi-GPU/TP. Crucially, the authors evaluated using the A100 hardware L2-residency control (cudaAccessPolicyWindow / persisting L2) as the reuse mechanism instead of registers+shared memory and measured roughly an 8% slowdown — i.e. explicit L2 residency was WORSE than their on-chip register/shared-memory caching, so L2 reuse is deliberately NOT the mechanism PERKS relies on.
scope_assumptions.zh: 鎖定迭代且受記憶體頻寬限制（bandwidth-bound 而非 compute-bound）的 kernel，其工作集不需要用盡所有 register/shared memory 即可達到尖峰效能；可重用容量受限於剩餘的晶片內 SRAM，因此問題必須能放進（或經 tiling 放進）可快取的子集。依賴 grid 層級 cooperative-group barrier（persistent grid 必須容納於單一 device）。為單 GPU，無多 GPU/TP。關鍵在於：作者曾改用 A100 硬體 L2 residency 控制（cudaAccessPolicyWindow / persisting L2）作為重用機制以取代 register+shared memory，量測到約 8% 的「變慢」——亦即顯式 L2 residency 比他們的晶片內 register/shared-memory 快取更差，因此 L2 reuse 刻意地並非 PERKS 所依賴的機制。

baselines_compared: AN5D / state-of-the-art stencil libraries, NVIDIA cuSPARSE-based CG (state-of-the-art Krylov/SpMV library), standard host-side iterative kernel-relaunch baseline

key_improvements.en: Geomean speedup 2.12x for 2D stencils and 1.24x for 3D stencils over state-of-the-art stencil libraries; for Conjugate Gradient, 4.86x geomean on smaller SuiteSparse SpMV datasets and 1.43x on larger datasets over a state-of-the-art library. Gains come from caching per-iteration output in leftover registers + shared memory to cut HBM traffic. Reuse/cache placement is central to the contribution, but the reuse tier is on-chip SRAM (registers + shared memory), NOT the L2 cache: the authors explicitly tried A100 L2 residency control as the caching mechanism and observed ~8% slowdown, confirming inter-kernel L2 reuse is not the effective lever here.
key_improvements.zh: 相較最先進的 stencil 函式庫，2D stencil 取得幾何平均 2.12x、3D stencil 1.24x 的加速；在 Conjugate Gradient 上，較最先進函式庫於較小的 SuiteSparse SpMV 資料集達 4.86x 幾何平均、較大資料集達 1.43x。加速來自把每次迭代的輸出快取在剩餘的 register 與 shared memory，以削減 HBM 流量。重用／快取放置是貢獻的核心，但重用層級是晶片內 SRAM（register + shared memory），而非 L2 cache：作者明確嘗試以 A100 L2 residency 控制作為快取機制，卻量到約 8% 的變慢，證實跨 kernel 的 L2 reuse 在此並非有效槓桿。

source.notes: L2-reuse relevance: reuse/caching across iterations is the entire mechanism, but the authors deliberately use on-chip registers+shared memory, NOT L2 residency; an explicit A100 L2-residency experiment gave ~8% slowdown.
